programmes.title: Basic Dementia Care Skill (Family) Course
programmes.shortIntro: To shift the daily caregiving focus away from rigid clinical routines and toward protecting personal dignity, emotional connection, and managing the progressive changes of dementia without burning out.
programmes.suitableFor: Family caregivers, relatives, community helpers, and those interested in or planning to further develop in dementia care.
programmes.description: Foundation Dementia Care Course for Family Caregivers covering 6 core modules, delivered by 12 ADFM-Certified Trainers with public healthcare experience. Pre-requisite for ADFM DCS-TTT certification. Limited to 100 seats only (subsidized from RM1,200 to RM120/pax). CPD points available.
programmes.language: English (with Malay & Chinese support where helpful)
highlights: Module 2 – Impact of Dementia & Person-Centred Care
Module 4 – Behavioural & Psychological Symptoms of Dementia (BPSD)
Module 6 – Legal, Ethical Issues & Advance Care Planning

programmes.title: Dementia Care Skill — Train the Trainer Program
programmes.roleCategory: Healthcare Professionals, Expert Educators & Senior Volunteers
programmes.shortIntro: The Train-the-Trainer (TTT) framework equipping and certifying healthcare professionals so they are equipped to deliver community DCS courses across Sarawak.
programmes.suitableFor: Selected healthcare professionals (nurses, therapists, medical officers), certified educators, and senior community volunteers.
programmes.description: An intensive 3-day certification curriculum under ADFM credentialing. Across 2024–2025, 4 cohorts have trained 68 frontline healthcare personnel across Kuching, Sibu, Bintulu and Miri to lead grassroots education.
programmes.language: English (with Bahasa Malaysia support provided where appropriate)
highlights: Comprehensive mastery of the community DCS curriculum & clinical nuances
Adult education techniques, group facilitation & interactive roleplays
Supervised mock teaching and clinical assessment under ADFM guidance
Accreditation as ADFM Certified Trainer listed in the public directory

programmes.title: Dementia Care Series — Care Worker
programmes.roleCategory: Professional Direct-Care Staff, Nursing Home Employees & Care Aides
programmes.shortIntro: A comprehensive workshop focused on building formal clinical competency. It establishes standard protocols for managing BPSD (Behavioral and Psychological Symptoms of Dementia), interpreting distress as communication, and mastering safe, person-centered physical handling.
programmes.suitableFor: Professional direct-care staff, nursing home employees, paid home nurses, assisted living attendants, and community health volunteers.
programmes.description: A rigorous, hands-on clinical training track crafted for institutional and community direct-care teams. Standardises compassionate clinical care, person-centred dementia support, and injury-free mobility assistance.
programmes.location: Kuching & Regional Healthcare Venues (To be announced)
highlights: Standard protocols for BPSD assessment & non-pharmacological de-escalation
Interpreting behavioural distress, agitation, and resistance as communication
Mastering safe, person-centred transfers & physical handling ergonomics
Institutional care dignity standards & care-plan documentation

roadmap.title: 1st Half Yearly Activity Calendar: "Finding The Missing Pieces"
roadmap.intro: Official calendar published by Rotary Club of Bintulu Central and ADFM, featuring key public webinars and dementia care skills training.

highlights.title: Webinar – Season 1 (Online)
highlights.desc: Online interactive session (80 minutes) focusing on understanding dementia and finding the missing pieces of community care.

highlights.title: Basic Dementia Care Skill (Family) Course (DCS-Family)
highlights.desc: Full-day training (9:00 AM – 6:00 PM) at Hock Lee Hotel & Residence, Kuching, equipping 100 family caregivers with practical bedside care skills.

highlights.title: Dementia Care Skill – Train the Trainer Program (DCS-TTT)
highlights.desc: Three-day comprehensive Train-the-Trainer program in Kuching to expand the cadre of certified ADFM trainers across Sarawak.

roadmap.title: DCS-TTT State-Wide Rollout: "68 Healthcare Workers Trained"
roadmap.intro: Four completed cohorts of Dementia Care Skill Train-the-Trainer (DCS-TTT) programs across Sarawak documented in See Hua and Sin Chew Daily news.

highlights.title: Cohorts 1 & 2: Kuching & Sibu
highlights.desc: First 18 medical personnel trained in Kuching, followed by Cohort 2 in Sibu to build regional dementia care competence.

highlights.title: Cohort 3 & Bintulu Community Dialogue
highlights.desc: DCS-TTT training in Bintulu paired with a large-scale public dialogue on dementia at Bintulu Civic Centre with local community leaders.

highlights.title: Cohort 4: Miri (68 Total Certified)
highlights.desc: Final cohort of the initial phase conducted in Miri, successfully certifying 68 doctors, nurses, and allied healthcare professionals.

roadmap.title: Community Support Ecosystem: "Structured Care Pathways"
roadmap.intro: Collaborative mission between Rotary Club of Bintulu Central and Alzheimer’s Disease Foundation Malaysia (ADFM) to deliver certified dementia care education.

highlights.title: 9 Certified Trainers & 3 QA/QC Specialists
highlights.desc: Multidisciplinary team of certified clinical trainers delivering evidence-based dementia care modules with official CPD accreditation.

highlights.title: 6 Core Modules for Family Caregivers
highlights.desc: From understanding neurocognitive disorders and communication to behaviour management, daily living activities, and caregiver self-care.

highlights.title: Multilingual Community Dialogues
highlights.desc: Engaging local Sarawakian families in English, Bahasa Melayu, and Chinese dialects to eliminate stigma and foster supportive networks.

communityOutreach.mainTitle: Alzheimer’s Care Project: TTT Batch 2 in Sibu
communityOutreach.intro: Back in May, our Batch 2 TTT in Sibu brought together a group of passionate participants from Kapit, Betong, and Sibu, who dedicated three days to learning, practicing, and preparing to serve their communities.

stories.title: Alzheimer’s Care Project TTT Batch 2 (16/5/25 – 18/5/25)

stories.description: Participants from Kapit, Betong, and Sibu dedicated three days to learning, practicing, and preparing to serve their communities with evidence-based dementia care skills.

stories.title: Living Impact & Growing Caregiver Support
stories.subtitle: Sibu, Sarawak (16/5/25 – 18/5/25)
stories.description: Although months have passed, the impact, memories, and lessons from Sibu remain very much alive in the way trainers share their knowledge, caregivers feel supported, and communities open their hearts toward dementia care.

hero.title: Meet your facilitators.
hero.subtitle: Experienced medical professionals certified under the Dementia Care Series (DCS-TTT) framework — bringing real caregiving knowledge to every session.

trainersList.name: Dr. Mohd Asri Bin Mohd Aris
trainersList.institution: Klinik Kesihatan Batu Kawa (KK Batu Kawa)
trainersList.bio: Medical Officer at Klinik Kesihatan Batu Kawa. Certified in the ADFM DCS-TTT framework, specializing in primary care dementia education, family counseling, and clinic referral pathways.

trainersList.name: Dr. Idda Syafarina Binti Albar
trainersList.bio: Senior Medical Officer (UD43) at KK Tanah Putih. Dedicated to bridging community health clinics with elderly caregiver networks, conducting dementia education workshops, and managing chronic care integration.

trainersList.name: Catherine Suhani Bt Sulaiman
trainersList.bio: Health Assistant at KK Kota Samarahan. Certified DCS facilitator with deep grassroots community outreach experience, facilitating bilingual caregiver dialogues and practical hands-on care sessions.

trainersList.name: Patricia Nawai anak Wilfred Ellie
trainersList.bio: Nursing Sister at Hospital Sentosa. Extensive background in geriatric emergency triage, physical transfer mechanics, and managing dementia-related agitation with person-centered empathy.

trainersList.name: Pearly Chai Sing Yee
trainersList.bio: Physiotherapist at SGH specializing in geriatric mobility maintenance, falls prevention strategies, and gentle restorative physical therapy tailored for individuals living with neurocognitive disorders.

trainersList.name: Dr. Sharon Lau
trainersList.bio: Medical Officer at Sarawak General Hospital's Department of Psychiatry & Mental Health. Facilitates DCS workshops in multilingual settings, focusing on behavioral distress management and psychiatric support.

trainersList.name: Nur Atiqah Binti Morshidi
trainersList.bio: Certified Occupational Therapist specializing in cognitive stimulation activities, adaptive home modifications, and sensory integration for individuals experiencing memory decline.

trainersList.name: Jenny Kong
trainersList.bio: Consultant Psychologist conducting caregiver emotional resilience workshops, burnout prevention groups, and psychological debriefing for families navigating progressive dementia diagnoses.

trainersList.name: Sr. Lily Wong
trainersList.bio: Senior Nurse Educator leading hands-on DCS physical transfer, incontinence care, and palliative comfort skills training for community health attendants and family caregivers across Sarawak.

trainersList.name: Dr. Tiong Ing Khieng
trainersList.bio: President of ADFM and clinical lead for the national DCS-TTT curriculum. Directs training standards, trainer credentialing examinations, and nationwide dementia advocacy partnerships with Rotary Clubs.

trainersList.name: Dr. Teh Kok Keng
trainersList.institution: Pusat Jantung Sarawak & Sarawak General Hospital
trainersList.bio: Consultant Geriatrician and Internal Medicine Specialist at Sarawak Heart Centre and SGH. Provides clinical advisory governance for the DCS-TTT certification syllabus and state-wide geriatric guidelines.

trainersList.name: Dr. Ling Jia Nee
trainersList.bio: Consultant Geriatrician at Sarawak General Hospital. Master clinical advisor overseeing complex BPSD protocols, ethical caregiving frameworks, and academic evaluation for the RCBC HopeCare initiative.
